target.baseline: Recent local summaries were still weak: autocurriculum stayed at active size 4 with episode_return around 0.42, and the latest forage-style 25x25-level summary showed about 0.16 return with two deliveries.

experiments.title: Small dense progress reward without actor oracle inputs
experiments.hypothesis: The 25x25 failure may be sparse navigation feedback. A tiny trainer-side distance-progress bonus can teach food-seeking and hub-return trajectories while leaving actor observations unchanged.
experiments.intervention: Use distance_bonus 0.02, gamma 0.997, concentrated food, moving writes, and the standard 4x4 to 25x25 staged ladder.
experiments.success_signal: Held-out 25x25 evaluation should show a large jump in delivered food and episode return, not merely more pickups.
experiments.report_notes: If this wins, report it as reward-shaping for credit density rather than an easier observation space.

experiments.title: Four ants with the same local policy
experiments.hypothesis: The scale cliff is partly exploration throughput: one ant rarely sees enough food-hub transitions on 20x20-25x25 maps. Four ants should produce more pickups and deliveries without giving the actor oracle coordinates.
experiments.intervention: Increase num_ants from 1 to 4 while keeping radius-1 local observations, moving writes, concentrated food, and the long-horizon gamma profile.
experiments.success_signal: At 25x25, deliveries and evaluation return should be several times the single-ant baseline; remaining food should fall sharply.
experiments.report_notes: This isolates embodied parallel exploration from observation changes.

experiments.title: Distance shaping plus four-ant exploration
experiments.hypothesis: DISTANCE_SHAPE proved dense progress reward can transfer to 25x25, but sampled evaluation still lagged deterministic evaluation. Adding four ants should improve coverage and make the shaped route behavior less brittle under sampled actions.
experiments.intervention: Keep distance_bonus 0.02 from the winning run and add four ants, hidden size 192, moving writes, concentrated food, and the same 25x25 stage ladder.
experiments.success_signal: Held-out 25x25 sampled delivery should close the gap with deterministic delivery while deterministic delivery remains above the DISTANCE_SHAPE baseline.
experiments.report_notes: Second-wave combination after DISTANCE_SHAPE: tests whether the remaining weakness is exploration throughput rather than reward density.

experiments.title: Distance plus four ants with low-entropy sharpening
experiments.hypothesis: DISTANCE_CAP4 and DISTANCE_VISION2_CAP4 both fully clear 25x25 when actions are sampled, but greedy argmax is brittle. The useful behavior is in the learned distribution, so lowering entropy pressure and giving late stages more consolidation budget may move the route actions onto the argmax path without removing the exploration benefits of four ants.
experiments.intervention: Keep the best sampled recipe from DISTANCE_CAP4: distance_bonus 0.02, four ants, radius-1 actor vision, hidden size 192, moving writes, and random layouts. Reduce ent_coef to 0.001, tighten clip_coef to 0.15, and run 1500 updates on high-end stages.
experiments.success_signal: The sampled 25x25 evaluation should remain near full clearance while deterministic delivered food rises meaningfully above DISTANCE_CAP4's 2.75-delivery greedy result.
experiments.report_notes: Tests whether the remaining problem is policy-selection sharpness rather than navigation skill; a win would justify reporting sampled and greedy metrics separately.

experiments.title: Distance plus four ants with moderate entropy sharpening
experiments.hypothesis: DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP greatly improved greedy delivery but slightly reduced sampled full-clear performance. A moderate entropy coefficient may preserve more stochastic exploration while still sharpening the useful route actions enough for greedy evaluation.
experiments.intervention: Use the same standard 25x25 distribution and late-stage consolidation as DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP, but set ent_coef to 0.003 rather than 0.001 while keeping clip_coef 0.15.
experiments.success_signal: Beat DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP's extended balance by keeping deterministic delivery near or above 16 while pushing sampled delivery back to a clean 23-food full-clear regime.
experiments.report_notes: Tests the entropy tradeoff directly after discovering that low entropy improves greedy behavior but weakens live large-stage training.

experiments.title: Winning sharp policy on a fine 20-to-25 ladder
experiments.hypothesis: DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP is the current best 25x25 policy, but its greedy behavior still falls short of full clearance. The late curriculum may be asking for too large a transfer jump, so a denser 20,21,22,23,24,25 ladder should reduce forgetting while preserving the low-entropy policy sharpening that already helped greedy evaluation.
experiments.intervention: Start from the same standard 25x25 task distribution as DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP: distance_bonus 0.02, four ants, radius-1 actor vision, hidden size 192, ent_coef 0.001, clip_coef 0.15, moving writes, random food, and random hub. Only change the stage schedule by adding dense high-end sizes, with 1300 updates on late stages to keep the run proper without over-spending relative to the winner.
experiments.success_signal: Beat DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP on held-out 25x25 balance: deterministic delivery should rise above 16 while sampled delivery should remain near full clearance.
experiments.report_notes: Tests curriculum smoothness on top of the current best recipe. A win would support reporting late-stage transfer as the remaining bottleneck rather than entropy, visibility, or ant count.

experiments.title: Warm-start sampled solver and sharpen on 25x25
experiments.hypothesis: DISTANCE_CAP4 already solves held-out 25x25 when actions are sampled, but its greedy argmax delivers only 2.75 food. The smarter next test is to keep the sampled-solver weights and do a gentle 25x25-only low-entropy fine-tune so existing route probability mass moves onto the argmax path.
experiments.intervention: Load the completed DISTANCE_CAP4 25x25 checkpoint, train only the standard 25x25 distribution for 1600 updates, keep distance_bonus 0.02 and four ants, lower entropy to 0.0005, tighten clip_coef to 0.10, use update_epochs 6, and reduce learning_rate to 0.00008 to avoid wiping out the sampled solver.

experiments.title: Warm-start best greedy checkpoint with deterministic rollouts
experiments.hypothesis: The best sampled policies solve 25x25, but standard sampled PPO rollouts do not reliably improve argmax behavior. experiments.title: Warm-start best checkpoint with mixed sampled and greedy rollouts
experiments.hypothesis: Pure greedy rollouts improved deterministic delivery less than hoped and weakened training return, while sampled warm-starts preserve full 25x25 solving. experiments.hypothesis: Sampled policies solve 25x25 but greedy argmax remains brittle. experiments.title: Warm-start best checkpoint on shorter 25x25 cookie routes
experiments.hypothesis: The standard 25x25 distribution may fail greedily because long source-hub routes compound small argmax errors. experiments.title: Warm-start best checkpoint with longer credit horizon
experiments.hypothesis: The policy often picks up food but greedy deployment fails to finish enough long return trips. Higher gamma, higher GAE lambda, and longer rollouts may give PPO a cleaner value target for carrying food back to the hub without changing task geometry or observations.

experiments.title: Gently align the long-credit sampled solver with greedy deployment
experiments.hypothesis: The extended evaluation shows the long-credit policy nearly solves shuffled 25x25 when actions are sampled, but the argmax path delivers far less. This suggests the policy distribution contains good return routes whose probability mass has not moved onto the mode. A small amount of greedy rollout pressure from the robust long-credit checkpoint should sharpen the useful route choices without repeating the earlier 25% greedy-pressure collapse from DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP.
experiments.intervention: Load the DISTANCE_CAP4_LONG_CREDIT_TUNE 25x25 checkpoint, train only the standard 25x25 distribution for 800 updates, keep gamma 0.999, gae_lambda 0.98, and num_steps 384, use deterministic_rollout_fraction 0.10, lower ent_coef to 0.0003, lower learning_rate to 0.00004, use clip_coef 0.10, and keep four ants with distance_bonus 0.02.

experiments.title: Collapse successful sampled routes toward argmax with entropy penalty
experiments.hypothesis: The best current policies clear shuffled 25x25 almost perfectly when sampled, so successful trajectories already exist in the policy distribution. The remaining failure is that deterministic argmax does not reliably choose those route actions. A small negative entropy coefficient should penalize diffuse action distributions and concentrate successful sampled behavior onto the mode without forcing every rollout action to be greedy.
experiments.intervention: Load the DISTANCE_CAP4_LONG_CREDIT_GENTLE_GREEDY checkpoint, train only the standard 25x25 distribution for 600 updates, keep gamma 0.999, gae_lambda 0.98, and num_steps 384, set ent_coef to -0.0005, use a conservative learning_rate 0.00002 and clip_coef 0.08, and keep four ants with distance_bonus 0.02.
experiments.success_signal: The strengthened 8+8 held-out gate should beat 16/23 deterministic delivery while sampled delivery remains near 23/23.
experiments.report_notes: Tests whether explicit entropy minimization is a cleaner argmax-alignment mechanism than greedy rollout mixing. This keeps the task distribution fixed and changes only the policy regularization pressure.

experiments.title: Re-run the winning sharp recipe with steadier high-stage optimization
experiments.hypothesis: The strongest robust policy so far is still the from-scratch low-entropy SHARP run, while every warm-start fine-tune preserved sampled solving but failed to improve argmax reliably. That suggests the useful deterministic route mode emerges during the full curriculum, not during local 25x25 polishing. A steadier SHARP run with lower learning rate, tighter PPO clipping, and more high-stage consolidation may improve deterministic generalization without sacrificing the sampled solver.

experiments.success_signal: The strengthened 8+8 held-out gate should beat DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP, with deterministic delivery above 16/23 and sampled delivery still above 22/23.

experiments.title: Combine radius-2 local vision with the winning sharp optimizer
experiments.hypothesis: Radius-2 actor vision plus four ants already produced a strong sampled 25x25 solver, but it had zero deterministic delivery when trained with higher entropy. The original SHARP recipe is the only robust argmax-improving family so far. Combining radius-2 local context with the same low-entropy SHARP optimizer may improve route stability and greedy delivery without losing sampled clearance.

experiments.title: Fine-tune SHARP by aligning only the movement head
experiments.hypothesis: Hybrid action evaluation shows sampled movement with greedy writing clears 25x25 near perfectly, while greedy movement with sampled writing remains much weaker. The deterministic bottleneck is therefore the movement head, not the write head. A small amount of movement-only greedy rollout pressure should align route movement choices with argmax while preserving the sampled/greedy write behavior that already works.

experiments.report_notes: Tests a targeted movement-head alignment mechanism motivated by the hybrid action diagnostic. This deliberately avoids full greedy rollout pressure because earlier both-head greedy and mixed-rollout fine-tunes damaged robust argmax performance.

experiments.title: Replicate the winning SHARP recipe with a second seed
experiments.hypothesis: The low-entropy SHARP curriculum is still the strongest robust deterministic policy, while fine-tunes and observability changes mostly preserve sampled solving but fail argmax. The remaining variance may come from the full curriculum trajectory and initialization seed. Re-running the exact winning recipe with a second seed tests whether a better deterministic mode can emerge without changing the algorithm.

experiments.title: Evaluate SHARP with sampled movement and greedy writing
experiments.hypothesis: The hybrid action diagnostic showed the bottleneck is the movement head: sampled movement with greedy writing nearly cleared 25x25, while greedy movement stayed brittle even when writing was sampled. The smartest near-term improvement may therefore be a deployment policy that samples route movement while taking the write head greedily, rather than forcing both heads through argmax.

experiments.title: Tune movement sampling temperature for SHARP deployment
experiments.hypothesis: The 32-episode hybrid gate confirmed that sampled movement with greedy writing clears almost all 25x25 cookies, while greedy movement loses route diversity. A lower movement temperature may keep enough stochastic routing to escape brittle argmax traps while reducing random dithering and improving completion speed/success.

experiments.title: Fine paired sweep around the best movement temperatures
experiments.hypothesis: The first movement-temperature sweep found that temperatures 1.00 and 1.25 both beat the untuned hybrid-policy gate, but the comparison used different seed streams per temperature. A paired-seed fine sweep should separate true temperature effects from layout variance and may find a better speed/success tradeoff around 1.10-1.25.

experiments.success_signal: A fine temperature should beat the previous best: delivered food above 22.66/23, success rate above 87.5%, or the same delivery with shorter episodes than temp 1.00.

A larger held-out gate should confirm whether this is robust enough to report as the recommended policy.

experiments.title: Four-ant speed fine-tune with an 800-step horizon
experiments.hypothesis: The best deployment policy clears 25x25 but takes about 1715 steps because training never paid for time. A warm-start fine-tune with a shorter episode cap and a small per-ant step penalty should preserve full clearance while forcing the colony to abandon dithering and repeated partial routes.

experiments.title: Four-ant direct 4x speed target at 550 steps

Failure here would indicate a physical throughput or exploration bottleneck rather than merely weak incentives.

If the remaining gap is collection throughput rather than route knowledge, a twelve-ant shared policy should raise delivered food inside the same 550-step cap without needing a different observation space.

experiments.title: Temperature sweep for the sixteen-ant speed checkpoint

The policy may need a different movement sampling temperature under the denser colony: lower temperature could reduce dithering, while higher temperature could spread workers to untouched sources.

experiments.title: Twenty-four-ant horizon ramp to the true 4x target
experiments.hypothesis: The sixteen-ant policy gets close to full delivery around 490 steps, but the actual 4x target from the current 1715-step behavior is about 430 steps. Reaching that target likely requires both more parallel workers and a gradual horizon curriculum so the colony learns to finish routes before the cap instead of merely collecting partial food.
experiments.intervention: Load the four-ant DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP checkpoint into a twenty-four-ant critic and train three explicit 25x25 stages with max_steps 700, then 550, then 430. Keep the standard food distribution, distance_bonus 0.02, low entropy, gamma 0.995, and a per-ant-scaled step_penalty 0.000045.
experiments.success_signal: A reportable win must deliver at least 22/23 food with mean episode length at or below 430. That would satisfy the requested 4x speedup while preserving near-complete 25x25 clearing.
experiments.report_notes: This is the first experiment aimed squarely at the true 4x threshold. It combines the observed benefit of ant-count scaling with a horizon ramp to avoid the direct-short-horizon under-delivery seen in the 4-, 8-, 12-, and 16-ant tests.

experiments.title: Twenty-four ants with less crowded food sources at 430 steps
experiments.hypothesis: The 24-ant 430-step ramp reached the requested speed but plateaued around 20.5/23 delivered food. With 24 workers and only six food-source tiles, the remaining loss may be source contention and redundant travel. Doubling the source count should let more ants collect in parallel while keeping total food, map size, and the 430-step target fixed.
experiments.intervention: Warm-start from DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP, expand to 24 ants, and repeat the 700->550->430 horizon ramp on 25x25 with 23 total food split across 12 food sources instead of 6. Keep cookie_distance 11, distance_bonus 0.02, low entropy, and step_penalty 0.000045.
experiments.success_signal: A win should beat the 6-source 24-ant ramp by delivering at least 22/23 food while keeping mean episode length at or below 430.
experiments.report_notes: This changes food-source distribution to reduce crowding. If it wins, report the mechanism as parallel source access plus horizon compression, not as a direct same-distribution improvement.

experiments.title: Polish the 24-ant 12-source checkpoint at the 430-step cap
experiments.hypothesis: The 24-ant 12-source ramp nearly satisfies the 4x target, delivering 21.35/23 at about 402 steps. The remaining gap may be final-stage consolidation rather than a new mechanism, because training still produced near-full fast episodes. A conservative polish should raise delivery without lengthening the policy.
experiments.intervention: Load the DISTANCE_CAP24_SPEED_SOURCES12_430 checkpoint and train only the 25x25, 12-source, max_steps-430 stage for 700 updates. Use lower learning_rate 0.00003, lower ent_coef 0.0003, and the same step_penalty 0.000045 to consolidate fast routes without destabilizing the near-miss policy.
experiments.success_signal: A win must cross 22/23 delivered while keeping mean episode length at or below 430. The main comparison is the parent checkpoint's 21.35/23 at 401.7 steps.
experiments.report_notes: This is a continuation polish of the best true-4x near miss. If it wins, report the recipe as 24 ants plus 12-source distribution plus final 430-step consolidation.

experiments.title: Fine movement-temperature sweep for the polished 4x checkpoint
experiments.hypothesis: The polished 24-ant, 12-source checkpoint nearly crosses the reportable threshold, with temperature 1.00 delivering 21.984/23 at about 397 steps. A fine sweep around 1.00 may recover the last fraction of a food item without changing training or task distribution.
experiments.intervention: Do not retrain. Load the DISTANCE_CAP24_SPEED_SOURCES12_POLISH_430 checkpoint and evaluate sampled movement with greedy writes at temperatures 0.95, 1.00, 1.05, and 1.10 over 96 same-seed shuffled 25x25 episodes.
experiments.success_signal: A winning temperature should deliver at least 22/23 food while keeping mean episode length at or below 430, confirming a reportable 4x-speed deployment policy.
experiments.report_notes: This is a deployment-only fine sweep on the best near-miss checkpoint. If it wins, report the final policy as the polished 24-ant, 12-source model with the selected movement temperature.

experiments.title: Final low-penalty polish for the 24-ant 12-source 430-step policy
experiments.hypothesis: The polished checkpoint is fast enough but repeatedly misses the 22/23 threshold by a tiny margin. Because the hard max_steps cap already enforces the 4x speed target, slightly reducing the per-step penalty may let PPO favor completing the last routes instead of trading them away for marginal speed.
experiments.intervention: Load the DISTANCE_CAP24_SPEED_SOURCES12_POLISH_430 checkpoint and run one more 25x25, 12-source, max_steps-430 stage for 500 updates. Keep the hard horizon, reduce step_penalty from 0.000045 to 0.000035, lower learning_rate to 0.00002, and use low entropy plus tight PPO clipping.
experiments.success_signal: A win should cross 22/23 delivered while mean episode length stays below 430. It should preserve the polished checkpoint's roughly 385-400 step regime while improving final-food completion.
experiments.report_notes: This is a final conservative polish of the best 4x-speed checkpoint. It changes only the fine-tuning pressure, not ant count, source count, or max horizon.

experiments.title: Completion-bonus polish for the last missed food at 430 steps
experiments.hypothesis: The best 24-ant, 12-source, 430-step policies are fast enough but repeatedly average just below 22/23 delivered. The environment currently gives no special reward for complete clearance beyond the final delivery itself, so the policy may rationally trade away the last difficult pickup/return. A one-time completion bonus should push the learned policy toward full clears while the hard 430-step cap preserves speed.
experiments.intervention: Add completion_bonus 2.0 and fine-tune the DISTANCE_CAP24_SPEED_SOURCES12_POLISH_430 checkpoint for one 25x25, 12-source, max_steps-430 stage. Keep the previous step_penalty 0.000045, low entropy, tight PPO clipping, and conservative learning_rate 0.00002.
experiments.success_signal: A win should exceed 22/23 delivered with mean episode length below 430 and improve success rate over the parent checkpoint's 50-52% range.
experiments.report_notes: This is a targeted reward-shaping polish for final completion. It preserves the same 24-ant, 12-source, 430-step task used by the near-miss policy, adding only an all-food completion incentive during training.

experiments.title: Short completion-bonus polish before over-training drift
experiments.hypothesis: The 500-update completion-bonus polish showed very strong early training updates but the final saved checkpoint regressed below the best near-miss delivery. The useful effect may be a brief final-clear nudge that over-trains if run too long.
experiments.intervention: Load the DISTANCE_CAP24_SPEED_SOURCES12_POLISH_430 checkpoint and train the same 25x25, 12-source, max_steps-430 completion-bonus stage for only 75 updates. Keep completion_bonus 2.0 and conservative optimizer settings, then evaluate the saved short-polish checkpoint at temperatures 0.95 and 1.00.
experiments.success_signal: A win should cross 22/23 delivered while keeping mean episode length below 430. It should beat both the parent checkpoint and the 500-update completion-bonus final checkpoint.
experiments.report_notes: This tests early stopping as a training-control parameter for completion shaping. It is motivated by the observed high early returns in the longer completion-bonus run.

experiments.title: Twenty-four ants with two dense food sources at the 430-step target
experiments.hypothesis: The fast 24-ant policies may be losing the final foods because the colony spreads over too many weak source routes and does not communicate well enough to coordinate cleanup. Concentrating the same 23 food units into only two source positions should create repeated high-value routes that many ants can exploit without needing broad exploration.
experiments.intervention: Keep total food at 23 and the 25x25 map fixed, but reduce food_sources from 12 to 2. Warm-start from the best 24-ant speed checkpoint, adapt for 250 updates at max_steps 550, then consolidate for 500 updates at the true 430-step cap with completion_bonus 1.5.
experiments.success_signal: A win should exceed 22/23 delivered while keeping mean episode length below 430. If it beats the 12-source near miss, condensed food was the right distribution shift.
experiments.report_notes: This directly tests the user's condensed-food hypothesis: same total food, far fewer source positions, same ant count, and same hard 430-step speed target.

experiments.title: Dense two-source speed policy with stronger byte-trail incentives
experiments.hypothesis: The visual behavior suggests ants are not communicating much. With only two dense food sources, route markings should be useful: carrying ants can write trails, empty ants can follow byte-marked routes toward food, and the shared policy may coordinate cleanup faster than pure movement sampling.
experiments.intervention: Use the same 24-ant, two-source, 430-step target as DENSE2, but increase write_bits to 2 and enable byte-trail shaping: delivery_byte_trail_bonus 0.20, byte_follow_bonus 0.004, carrying_byte_write_bonus 0.002. Warm-start from the best 24-ant speed checkpoint and transfer the extra write bit with neutral-new initialization.
experiments.success_signal: A win should exceed the non-trail dense run on delivered food and success rate while staying below 430 mean steps. Increased byte usage should appear in W&B diagnostics rather than being a no-op.
experiments.report_notes: This tests communication explicitly rather than assuming more ants will solve coordination. It changes memory capacity and byte incentives while keeping the condensed food distribution fixed.

experiments.title: Twenty-four ants with sixteen food sources at the 430-step target
experiments.hypothesis: The condensed two-source experiments underperformed badly, while the 12-source policy is the strongest near miss. This suggests the 24-ant fast colony benefits from more independent pickup opportunities rather than fewer crowded source routes. Sixteen sources may reduce contention enough to cross 22/23 while keeping total food fixed at 23.
experiments.intervention: Keep 23 total food, 24 ants, and the hard 430-step target. Warm-start from the best 24-ant speed checkpoint, adapt to 16 food sources for 250 updates at max_steps 550, then consolidate for 500 updates at max_steps 430 with completion_bonus 1.5.
experiments.success_signal: A win should exceed 22/23 delivered with mean episode length below 430, beating both the 12-source near miss and the failed two-source condensed runs.
experiments.report_notes: This closes the food-source-count question raised by the condensed-food hypothesis. If it wins, the report should say the colony needs more parallel pickup sites, not more condensation.

experiments.title: Select the best mid-training 12-source speed checkpoint
experiments.hypothesis: Several speed polishes show high training-return spikes before the final checkpoint drifts lower. The current workflow always evaluates the terminal checkpoint, so it may discard the useful policy that briefly appears mid-run. Saving and selecting the best reported training checkpoint should recover that policy if drift, not capacity, is the main remaining bottleneck.
experiments.intervention: Load the strongest 24-ant, 12-source, 430-step checkpoint and fine-tune the same distribution for 700 updates. Save a rolling best checkpoint whenever logged episode_return improves, select that _best checkpoint for evaluation, and keep total food, source count, ant count, and horizon fixed.
experiments.success_signal: A win should exceed 22/23 delivered with mean episode length below 430 and beat the terminal-checkpoint 12-source polishes. If it wins, the report should emphasize checkpoint selection and training drift as the missing control parameter.
experiments.report_notes: This is not a new distribution or reward trick. It isolates whether the previous near-misses were caused by evaluating stale terminal checkpoints after useful mid-training policies had already appeared.

experiments.title: Thirty-two-ant final throughput push at 430 steps
experiments.hypothesis: The best 24-ant, 12-source policies repeatedly land just under 22/23 delivered while staying well below 430 steps. The remaining gap may be raw final pickup and return throughput. Expanding the polished 24-ant checkpoint to 32 shared-policy ants should increase parallel route coverage without changing the successful 12-source distribution or the 430-step cap.
experiments.intervention: Load the DISTANCE_CAP24_SPEED_SOURCES12_POLISH_430 checkpoint, expand the critic to 32 ants, and fine-tune one 25x25, 12-source, max_steps-430 stage for 600 updates. Use a per-ant-scaled step_penalty 0.00003, low entropy, and conservative PPO settings.
experiments.success_signal: A win should finally exceed 22/23 delivered while keeping mean episode length below 430. If it does not beat the 24-ant policies, ant-count scaling has saturated for this distribution.
experiments.report_notes: This is a targeted throughput test from the best near-miss checkpoint. It changes only the colony size and final-stage fine-tuning pressure while preserving the 12-source 430-step target.

experiments.title: Eight-ant horizon ramp from 900 to 550 steps
experiments.hypothesis: The direct 550-step eight-ant run improved speed but failed to preserve full clearance. A smoother horizon curriculum should first let the transferred eight-ant colony learn fast complete routes at 900 and 700 steps, then compress to the 550-step target without abruptly erasing delivery behavior.
experiments.intervention: Load the four-ant DISTANCE_CAP4_SHARP checkpoint into an eight-ant critic and train three explicit 25x25 stages: max_steps 900, then 700, then 550. Keep the same standard food distribution, distance_bonus 0.02, low entropy, gamma 0.995, and a per-ant-normalized step_penalty 0.00012.
experiments.success_signal: Beat the direct eight-ant 550 run by preserving higher delivery while ending near the 550-step cap. The target remains at least 22/23 delivered with mean episode length below 650, then below 550 if successful.
experiments.report_notes: This tests autocurriculum-like compression of episode horizon while keeping size and food distribution fixed. It is the clean follow-up if direct short-horizon pressure caused under-delivery.

experiments.title: Distance shaping plus four ants and radius-2 vision
experiments.hypothesis: If DISTANCE_CAP4 helps but still misses full completion, the remaining bottleneck may be local route stability. Radius-2 vision should help ants preserve useful trajectory context while the distance bonus supplies dense credit.
experiments.intervention: Combine distance_bonus 0.02, four ants, radius-2 actor vision, hidden size 256, moving writes, and the same 25x25 stage ladder.
experiments.success_signal: This candidate should push deterministic 25x25 delivery toward full clearance and improve sampled delivery beyond DISTANCE_CAP4.
experiments.report_notes: Higher-upside combined run; less ablated, but directly targets the two remaining suspected bottlenecks.

experiments.title: Single ant with radius-2 local vision
experiments.hypothesis: Radius-1 vision may be too myopic once the map grows; the policy cannot stabilize trajectories because landmarks vanish immediately. Radius-2 vision gives a larger local context without direct food or hub coordinates.
experiments.intervention: Increase actor_vision_radius from 1 to 2, keep one ant, keep the same staged 25x25 gate, and use the long-horizon gamma profile.
experiments.success_signal: 25x25 pickups should rise first; if delivery also rises, local observability was a core bottleneck.
experiments.report_notes: This is the cleanest observation-capacity test because it changes only what the actor can locally see.

experiments.title: Shorter source-hub distances during scale-up
experiments.hypothesis: The learner may fail because larger stages make first successful delivery loops too rare. Shorter cookie distances should increase complete pickup-delivery examples while still requiring navigation on 25x25.
experiments.intervention: Scale per-stage cookie_distance by 0.5, preserve total food and random layouts, and keep all policy/trainer parameters otherwise close to baseline.
experiments.success_signal: If delivery improves much more than pickup, route-length distribution was the bottleneck.
experiments.report_notes: This explicitly tests cookie placement geometry, not model capacity.

experiments.title: Denser food sources for easier route consolidation
experiments.hypothesis: The ant may not get enough repeated local evidence for the same route when food is spread over many sources. Fewer, richer sources should make pickup-delivery behavior easier to consolidate before 25x25.
experiments.intervention: Keep total food per stage but set food_source_divisor to 8, so larger maps have fewer source tiles with more bites per source.
experiments.success_signal: 25x25 delivery_events should improve more than pickup_events; that would mean the agent is exploiting repeated source-hub trips.
experiments.report_notes: This tests distribution design rather than policy architecture.

experiments.title: Higher gamma with longer rollouts
experiments.hypothesis: The large-map failure may be credit assignment after pickup: delivery reward is too delayed relative to the rollout/value target. Higher gamma and longer rollouts should make carrying-to-hub behavior less brittle.
experiments.intervention: Use gamma 0.999, gae_lambda 0.98, num_steps 320, lower entropy, and fewer environments to keep the batch manageable.
experiments.success_signal: If pickups stay similar but deliveries rise at 20x20-25x25, delayed delivery credit was limiting learning.
experiments.report_notes: This is the pure trainer-budget/credit-assignment run.

experiments.title: Finer high-end stage ladder
experiments.hypothesis: The handoff from mid-size maps to 25x25 may be too abrupt. A ladder with dense stages from 18x18 through 25x25 should reduce forgetting and make final-stage behavior more stable.
experiments.intervention: Use stage sizes 4,6,8,10,12,15,18,20,21,22,23,24,25 with the standard long-horizon profile.
experiments.success_signal: Held-out 25x25 evaluation should improve even if per-stage training budgets are unchanged, indicating schedule smoothness matters.
experiments.report_notes: This tests curriculum size spacing directly.

experiments.title: Four ants plus radius-2 vision
experiments.hypothesis: If CAPACITY4 and VISION2 each help, the combination may pass the 25x25 gate decisively by improving both exploration throughput and local route stability.
experiments.intervention: Use four ants, radius-2 actor vision, hidden size 256, and the standard long-horizon profile.
experiments.success_signal: This should be the first candidate expected to exceed 5.0 return at 25x25 if the scale cliff is mostly data and observability.
experiments.report_notes: This is deliberately less ablated but higher upside.

experiments.title: Reward byte trails only when they support delivery
experiments.hypothesis: Moving writes may be present but unused because there is no immediate reason to create persistent route marks. Small trail/follow bonuses can make byte memory useful without rewarding arbitrary writing.
experiments.intervention: Add carrying_byte_write_bonus, byte_follow_bonus, and delivery_byte_trail_bonus while keeping one writable bit and moving writes.
experiments.success_signal: A winning run should increase delivery return and maintain or improve write-to-delivery usefulness, not just write entropy.
experiments.report_notes: This tests whether learned external memory helps long-horizon foraging.

experiments.title: Autocurriculum with active-size progress bonus
experiments.hypothesis: The fixed curriculum may overfit each size handoff. Autocurriculum can expose continuous active-size growth if we directly reward stage advancement and use a sane update budget.
experiments.intervention: Train one 50x50 autocurriculum run with stage_completion_bonus, gamma 0.997, radius-2 vision, and a proper but bounded update cap.
experiments.success_signal: The checkpoint should show higher autocurriculum active-size progress and more deliveries than the old single-ant baseline.
experiments.report_notes: This tests whether the curriculum schedule itself is the issue.
